document_type: Multi-SPEC Architecture Contract (SPEC-00 + SPEC-01 + SPEC-02 + SPEC-04)

findings.title: Persistent DHF session lock creates permanent availability failure requiring manual SQL intervention
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam C paragraph beginning 'DHF append failure locks the session persistently (never descopable)' and 'OpenOrResumeSessionAsync rejects locked sessions'; SPEC-04 §7.1 LockSessionAsync and §6.1 OpenOrResumeSessionCore
findings.evidence: 'The session is locked persistently by calling DhfLedger.LockSessionAsync... The lock survives orchestrator restart... Reopening requires manual intervention (operator closes the session via SQL)'
findings.problem: Transient DB outage, network blip to Railway, or AppendTurnAsync retry exhaustion locks the session forever; no automated unlock, no circuit-breaker, no operator dashboard.
findings.why_it_matters: In medtech production (explicitly targeted via SDR-TL-006 and Medtronic pitch) this violates availability; opposite assumption (transient faults occur) turns every fault into outage.
findings.proposed_fix: Add mandatory unlock API with audit trail plus configurable auto-unlock after operator notification; remove 'never descopable' gate until recovery UX exists.

findings.title: Viewer UUID capability as sole access control is brittle against leakage or sharing in adversarial sharing scenarios
findings.location: SPEC-00 SDR-TL-012 full text and 'The viewer does NOT auto-expose sessions without a session UUID'; SPEC-00 §2 'Viewer GET / without sessionId now renders neutral landing page'; SPEC-00 §6 'Tenant' definition
findings.evidence: 'Access control is "knowledge of the session UUID" — a UUIDv4 capability with ~122 bits of entropy... Session URLs are reachable by anyone who has the URL; knowing one session UUID for a tenant reveals all sessions for that tenant'
findings.problem: URLs are logged by browsers, proxies, analytics, screenshots, or forwarded in Medtronic 'look at the product' emails; no revocation, no tenant isolation on leak, no Clerk until v1.5.
findings.why_it_matters: Trade-secret CAD models or PHI-adjacent designs become public; 'acceptable for hackathon' claim contradicts Medtronic production goal and Part 11 governance language.
findings.proposed_fix: Make viewer auth mandatory for v1 with same 15-30 minute Clerk middleware; treat UUID-only as explicit defect rather than deferred feature.

findings.title: BSMS enforcement and 'no vector retrieval ever' SDR inflates complexity and creates brittle dependency on perfect structured schema for all future knowledge needs
findings.location: SPEC-00 SDR-TL-009 full text including 'Enforcement', 'Rationale' points 1-4, and 'CAD-BSMS roadmap' paragraph; cross-referenced in SPEC-00 §4 and SPEC-04 §0
findings.evidence: 'Architecture review for any runtime change... MUST verify the mechanism is BSMS-shaped. Reviewer checklist: (1) is there a domain-persona bouncer?... If any answer is no, the change is rejected. Locked. Applies to all descendants'
findings.problem: Hackathon deliverable only needs 9 tools against live SolidWorks state; mandating bouncer + Postgres vocabulary DB + dual Sonnet calls for every future term ('bore', 'lumen') before any implementation creates review friction and scope drift.
findings.why_it_matters: What if opposite assumption is true (vector retrieval with citations works for non-regulated demo)? Current rule turns every retrieval discussion into governance gate; NASA MIRA validation does not prove necessity for CAD feature names.
findings.proposed_fix: Scope SDR-TL-009 to post-v1 regulated vocabulary layer only; permit local vector cache for non-audited demo features with explicit testability exception.

findings.title: Threading and post-timeout recovery assumptions in Seam B are brittle against SolidWorks COM implementation changes or non-deterministic STA behavior
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam B 'Cancellation boundary' and 'Post-timeout recovery (mandatory — never descopable)' paragraphs; SPEC-02 §2.2, §2.4, and §2.6 StaCommandQueueTests description
findings.evidence: 'Once a synchronous COM call is in flight, it runs to completion; the STA thread cannot be safely interrupted... SPEC-03 defines the deterministic selection rule between the two permitted strategies (state refresh via feature-tree comparison, or undo-group rollback)'
findings.problem: Depends on exact SynchronizationContext behavior (Day-0 probe documented but not enforced), SolidWorks message pump never changing, and COM calls always terminating; no fallback if recovery comparison itself diverges.
findings.why_it_matters: Edge case of SolidWorks 2026 SPx altering UI thread or rebuild timing breaks mandatory never-descopable recovery, forcing locked sessions; architecture test cannot catch runtime nondeterminism.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit 'COM recovery cannot be guaranteed' disclaimer and degraded mode that forces full model reload on any timeout; remove 'deterministic selection rule' claim.

top_3_must_fix: Persistent DHF session lock on append failure (critical operational risk)
Viewer UUID-only access control (high security exposure for CAD data)
BSMS enforcement SDR creating unnecessary complexity for hackathon scope
